reason: The mechanism is real and the timings are accurate, but the three perceptual claims the consequence rests on are all measurably false, and stripping them leaves a refinement, not a defect. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?motion=play, sampling deterministically by pausing every animation and pinning currentTime (page.clock drifts the document timeline; the seat's numbers survive that correction). CONFIRMED: document.getAnimations() returns 0 animations whose target is .bar-val, in full and in first-run. The live bar (i=11) is animation-delay 0.78s / 0.5s, so lastBar height is 0.0px at T=780 and 168px at T=1280; in first-run the solo bar (i=0) is 0.34s/0.5s. Every number the seat quotes checks out. REFUTED on three counts. (1) 'at opacity 1, in its final place, from frame one' is false. The label lives inside .card.hero.rise, which is rise 0.5s backwards at 65ms. Measured card opacity: 0 at T=0, 0.288 at T=100, 0.805 at T=200, 0.978 at T=340 — and the label's own top is 293.0px at T=0, 290.1 at 100, 285.0 at 200, 283.0 at 500. So at frame one it is at opacity 0 and 10px below its final place; it arrives on the card's rise with the hero number, the delta pill, the sentence and the note, exactly like everything else in the card. It is not early to the frame — it is early to its column only. (2) 'hangs at the top of an empty plot with nothing beneath it' is false for state=full. Counting bars with painted height >1px: 0 at T=340, 4 at T=500, 7 at T=620, 11 at T=780. The plot is not empty for 780ms; it is mid-sweep, and the label sits over the last slot of a left-to-right sweep that has visibly reached it. In the 620ms frame the reader is watching columns arrive and the indigo label reads as the destination of the sweep, not as an orphan. (3) 'a floating indigo 12 so far over blank white' in first-run is false. At T=100/200/340 the card is at 0.288/0.805/0.978 opacity and carries the hero '12', 'jobs finished since you started, Harbour House weddings', the comparison-arrives note, the 57px baseline and the '13 JUL' tick, all rising together; the label is one element on a card that is itself arriving, and the actual first frame a new customer sees is opacity 0. What is left after the corrections is that the live week's value paints with the chart's LABEL RAIL rather than with its mark — and the rail is what the source says it belongs to (.chart comment, lately.html:243: 'A label rail on the right. The axis maximum, the previous-best tag and the live week's value all anchor to this edge'). The gridline value labels '12' and '6' are static and also present before any column exists, in the same band, 34px to the right. A rail label arriving with its scale is a defensible reading, not something visibly wrong. The .record-tag precedent does not carry the weight the seat puts on it either: a dashed rule that has not drawn leaves its tag pointing at nothing, whereas a right-rail value 6px above where its column will end is pointing at its own slot. SEVERITY overstated: this is 'refinement' (nothing is wrong), not 'defect' (visibly wrong but passable), and the brief makes an overstated class a reason to refute. THE FIX also fails on its own description and on first-run. Patched into a staged copy and measured: with --i emitted the live label computes animation-delay 1.24s in full and 0.8s in first-run, which is the arithmetic the seat claims. But 'it lands as the mark completes' is wrong — with a 0.35s rise starting at 1240ms the label reaches opacity 1 at 1590ms, measured 0.447 at T=1280 and 0.952 at T=1400, i.e. 310ms AFTER the column completes, not at it. And in first-run the fix is a net loss: the solo column is fully drawn at 840ms while the label is at 0.447 opacity and does not land until 1150ms, so the one screen the finding calls the new customer's first frame gains a ~300ms fully-opaque frame of a full-height indigo hatched column carrying no value at all, and the label becomes the last thing that moves on a card whose entire subject it is. Trading a label-without-mark for a mark-without-label on that exact screen, and stretching first-run's entrance from 840ms to 1150ms to do it, is not an improvement at this bar. To the seat's credit, two of its safety claims check out: no overprint was produced against .gridline b or .record-tag at any sampled entrance frame, and [data-motion="settled"], prefers-reduced-motion and [data-state="loading"] do zero the new animation, so no graded frame changes.
sharpenedFix: If the panel acts on this at all, act on full/partial/quiet only and tie the label to its column's completion rather than to a fixed 800ms base, and leave first-run alone — its solo column starts at 340ms and completes at 840ms, inside the card's own rise, and the label already lands with the card. Emit --i on the live label in chart() only (style="--h:${pct(w.v, max)};--i:${i}"), leave the first-run solo markup untouched at style="--h:100", and scope the rule so the solo plot is excluded: `.plot:not(.solo) .bar-val { animation: rise 0.3s var(--ease) backwards; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms + 640ms); }`. At i=11 that is 1080ms, when the column is at ~94% of its grow, landing at 1380ms — 100ms after the column completes at 1280ms and 120ms before the record-tag at 1500ms. That reproduces the record-tag precedent exactly (the tag starts at ~67% of its rule's draw and lands 200ms after it), keeps the entrance at its existing 1.9s, and never leaves a completed mark unlabelled. Note that the label with no --i emitted inherits --i:1 from .card.hero, so the scoping must be by selector, not by the absence of the custom property.
breaks: The gate that guards this area, 'no two chart labels overprint' / 'no chart label leaves its card' (interaction-check.mjs:631-658), opens every page with reducedMotion: true, so it measures rest geometry only. Any bar-val animation therefore ships entirely unmeasured at the entrance: I measured zero clashes against .gridline b and .record-tag at T=620/900/1240/1280/1400/1590/1900, but nothing in the suite would catch a regression, and the rest boxes are already close — .bar-val occupies y 283.0-297.9 and the max gridline's b occupies roughly y 290-304, separated only by the 34px --gutter horizontally. If any bar-val animation lands, that gate needs a driven-entrance companion assertion sampling the translateY(10px) backwards-fill position, or the 640ms/1080ms timing is protected by nothing. Also re-measure: the loading state's neutralisation at lately.html:1231 sets --h to 46 on .bar-val, and emitting --i there too must stay covered by [data-state="loading"] *, animation: none !important (verified today); the entrance-order assertion at interaction-check.mjs:534 ('the previous best draws last, after the columns have grown'); and both dark-twin and 390/768 widths, where the solo and last-child positioning rules for .bar-val differ.
